1.note:
# General Information:

Yahweh tells Ezekiel to speak a prophecy. Ezekiel is to speak to the mountains of Israel, but the message is for all of the people of Israel.

God calls Ezekiel this to emphasize that Ezekiel is only a human being. God is eternal and powerful, but humans are not. See how you translated this in [Ezekiel 2:1](ta:02). Alternate translation: [mortal person] or [human]

1.q: prophesy to the mountains of Israel
1.note: God wants Ezekiel to speak to the mountains as if they were people. The message is for the people of Israel.

2.note: This is an expression of joy. It can be translated as “I am very happy” or “This is great.”
“The very old mountains.” This refers to the high mountains of Israel.

3.note: If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea behind the word **desolation**, you can express the same idea with a verbal form such as “desolate.” Alternate translation: [Because you, mountains of Israel, have become desolate]

3.q: because of the attacks that came on you from all sides
3.note: Alternate translation: [because you were attacked from every direction] or [because your enemies attacked you from every direction]

3.q: you have been the subject of slanderous lips and tongues, and of people’s stories
3.note: Here, “lips” and “tongues” represent people speaking. Alternate translation: [people are saying bad things about you, and the nations are telling bad stories about you]

The word translated as **desolating** represents the standard written Hebrew text as we have it today. This reading, however, does not seem to make sense. Scholars have proposed that a scribe may have mistaken this word for a very similar word that means to gasp or pant. Combined with the following word, the result is a word pair that describes strong desire as “panting” for something. The UST follows that interpretation. You may want to follow the major translation in your area. Alternate translation: [of gasping and panting for]

4.q: listen to the word of the Lord Yahweh
4.note: Alternate translation: [listen to the message of the Lord Yahweh]

If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea behind the word **desolations**, you can express the same idea with a verbal form such as “desolate cities.” Alternate translation: [the desolate cities which have no people living in them]

If your language does not use the passive form in this way, you can state this in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [the cities that people have left behind]
Alternate translation: [that enemies have stolen from]

5.q: in the fire of my fury
5.note: This speaks of Yahweh’s fury as if it were a fire. Yahweh loves Israel very much, so he becomes jealous and angry when other nations mock it. Alternate translation: [because of my intense jealousy] or [because of my very strong anger]
Alternate translation: [and against all of Edom]

5.q: had both joy in their heart and disdain in their spirit, as they seized my land
5.note: Here “heart” and “spirit” represent a person’s inner being. The ideas of having joy and disdain can be expressed with the verbs “rejoiced” and “despised.” Alternate translation: [who despised the people of Israel and rejoiced while they took my land]

Following the custom of the culture, Yahweh is swearing an oath by stating the first part of a condition (“if”) but not the second part (“then”), which would be the penalty for not telling the truth. Normally the penalty would be understood to be something general such as “may Yahweh punish me severely,” yielding something like, “If it was not in the fire of my jealousy that I have spoken against…, may Yahweh punish me severely…” But since Yahweh is speaking, stating this would not make sense. It may be clearest to translate the oath as a positive statement, as in the UST.

6.note: The word “Behold” here adds emphasis to what follows. Alternate translation: [Indeed!]

6.q: In my fury and in my anger
6.note: The words “fury” and “anger” mean basically the same thing. Together they emphasize the intensity of his anger. Alternate translation: [Because I am extremely angry]

6.q: you have borne the insults of nations
6.note: Alternate translation: [other nations have insulted you] or [other nations have mocked you]

7.note: Here **I have lifted up my hand** is a symbolic action that shows that a person is taking an oath. Alternate translation: [I solemnly swear]

7.q: that the nations that surround you will certainly carry their own shame
7.note: The people experiencing shame are spoken of as if they will carry their shame. Alternate translation: [that people will certainly mock the nations that surround you]
The word “you” refers to the mountains of Israel.

Following the custom of the culture, Yahweh is swearing an oath by stating the first part of a condition (“if”) but not the second part (“then”), which would be the penalty for not telling the truth. Normally the penalty would be understood to be something general such as “may Yahweh punish me severely,” yielding something like, “If the nations that are around you will not bear their humiliation, may Yahweh punish me severely…” But since Yahweh is speaking, stating this would not make sense. It may be clearest to translate the oath as a positive statement, as in the UST.

8.q: you will grow branches and bear fruit
8.note: Here “you” refers to the mountain of Israel which here represents the trees on the mountain that will grow fruit. Alternate translation: [your trees will grow branches and bear fruit]

9.note: Alternate translation: [pay attention, because what I am about to say is both true and important: I]
“I want to do good things to you.” The word “you” refers to the mountains of Israel.
Alternate translation: [I will be kind to you]

9.q: you will be plowed and sown with seed
9.note: If your language does not use the passive form in this way, you can state this in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [my people, Israel, will plow your ground and sow it with seed]

10.q: So I will multiply upon you
10.note: Yahweh is speaking to the mountains. This can be stated explicitly. Alternate translation: [So, mountains of Israel, I will multiply upon you]

10.q: even the whole house of Israel
10.note: Here “house” represents people. Alternate translation: [all of the people of Israel]

10.q: The cities will be inhabited and the ruins rebuilt
10.note: If your language does not use the passive form in this way, you can state this in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [Then people will live in the cities and will rebuild the ruins]

11.q: they will multiply and be fruitful
11.note: Here “be fruitful” is an idiom that means to have many children and descendants. Alternate translation: [they will become very many people and have very many children]

11.q: you to be inhabited as you previously were
11.note: If your language does not use the passive form in this way, you can state this in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [people to live on you mountains as they did before]

When Yahweh says that people will know that he is Yahweh, he is implying that they will know that he is the one true God who has supreme authority and power. See how you translated this in Ezekiel 6:7. Alternate translation: [understand that I am Yahweh, the one true God] or [realize that I, Yahweh, have supreme power and authority]

12.q: They will possess you, and you will be their inheritance
12.note: The people living in the mountains and land of Israel permanently is spoke of as if the people would inherit them. Alternate translation: [They will possess you permanently]

12.q: you will no longer cause their children to die
12.note: It is implied that in the past children died because there was not enough food in the land. Now the land would produce enough food.

13.note: Alternate translation: [other nations are saying to you mountains]
Not enough food growing in Israel so that people die is spoken of as if the mountains of Israel were devouring the people. Alternate translation: [You cause many people to die]
Alternate translation: [you cause your people’s children to die]

14.q: you will not consume people any longer
14.note: Not enough food growing in Israel so that people die is spoken of as if the mountains of Israel were consuming the people. Alternate translation: [you will no longer cause the people to die]

14.q: This is the Lord Yahweh’s declaration
14.note: Yahweh speaks of himself by name to express the certainty of what he is declaring. See how you translated this in Ezekiel 5:11. Alternate translation: [This is what the Lord Yahweh has declared] or [This is what I, the Lord Yahweh, have declared]

The phrase **cause to stumble** is a translation of the standard written Hebrew text as we have it today. There is, however, a correction in the margin of the text that Hebrew scribes have recommended, which the UST follows. You may want to follow this correction in your translation, or you may want to follow the major translation in your area. Alternate translation: [you will not be bereaved of]

15.q: Nor will I allow you to hear the insults of the nations any longer
15.note: This speaks of the mountains as if they were able to hear when people insult them. Alternate translation: [I will no longer allow the other nations to insult you]

15.q: you will no longer have to bear the shame of the peoples
15.note: Experiencing shame is spoken of as if the mountains could bear shame. Alternate translation: [the peoples will no longer cause you to feel ashamed] (See also: [Metaphor](ta:figs-metaphor))

16.note: This is an idiom that is used to introduce something that God told his prophets or his people. See how you translated this in Ezekiel 3:16. Alternate translation: [Yahweh spoke this message] or [Yahweh spoke these words]

17.note: God calls Ezekiel this to emphasize that Ezekiel is only a human being. God is eternal and powerful, but humans are not. See how you translated this in [Ezekiel 2:1](ta:02). Alternate translation: [Mortal person] or [Human]
Here “house” represents people. Alternate translation: [the people of Israel]

17.q: with their ways and their deeds
17.note: Alternate translation: [by the way they lived and the things they did]

17.q: Their ways were like the unclean menstruation of a woman before me
17.note: This compares how the people behaved to a woman’s unclean menstruation rags. This emphasizes how disgusting their behaviors were to Yahweh. Alternate translation: [Their ways were as disgusting to me as the unclean menstruation of a woman]
the time every month when a woman bleeds from her womb

18.q: I poured out my fury against them
18.note: Yahweh punishing people because he is angry is spoken of as if his fury were a liquid that he poured out. Alternate translation: [I did things to them that showed how angry I was]

18.q: for the blood that they poured out on the land
18.note: This is an idiom that refers to killing someone. Alternate translation: [because they made the blood of many people spill onto the land] or [because they murdered many people]

18.q: for their pollution of it by their idols
18.note: The people worshiping idols is spoken of as if the idols made the land physically dirty. Alternate translation: [because they defiled the land with their idols]

19.q: I scattered them among the nations; they were dispersed through the lands
19.note: These two phrases mean basically the same thing. See how you translated a similar phrase in Ezekiel 12:15. Alternate translation: [I caused them to separate and live in separate lands]

19.q: they were dispersed through the lands
19.note: If your language does not use the passive form in this way, you can state this in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [I dispersed them through the lands]
Here “ways” and “deeds” mean basically the same thing. Alternate translation: [the things that they have done]

20.note: Here, **the name of my holiness** represents Yahweh himself, who is holy. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [me, who is holy]

Yahweh is using the possessive form to describe a **name** that is characterized by **holiness**. If a speaker of your language would not use the possessive form for this, you could express this idea in another way. Alternate translation: [my name, which is holy]

20.q: Are these really the people of Yahweh?
20.note: The people use a question to express their surprise at what they saw. Alternate translation: [I cannot believe these are really the people of Yahweh!]

20.q: For they have been thrown out of his land
20.note: If your language does not use the passive form in this way, you can state this in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [For Yahweh has forced them out of his land]
This refers to the land of Israel.

21.q: But I had compassion for my holy name that the house of Israel had defiled among the nations, when they went there
21.note: Here “name” represents Yahweh and his reputation. Alternate translation: [When the house of Israel went among the nations, they caused me disgrace, but I wanted people to know that I am holy]

21.q: I had compassion for my holy name
21.note: Alternate translation: [I cared about my holy name]
Here “house” represents people. Alternate translation: [the people of Israel]

22.note: Here “house” represents people. Alternate translation: [the people of Israel]
Alternate translation: [because of you] or [in order to help you]

22.q: but for my holy name, which you have profaned among the nations everywhere you have gone
22.note: Here “name” represents Yahweh and his reputation. Alternate translation: [but so that the people of the nations, who mock me because of you, will know that I am holy]

22.q: you have profaned among the nations everywhere you have gone
22.note: Alternate translation: [you have caused the people of the nations to mock everywhere you have gone]

25.q: I will sprinkle pure water on you so you will be purified from all of your impurities, and I will purify you from all of your idols
25.note: Yahweh forgiving the people and causing them to no longer sin is spoken of as if he would cleanse them with water. The phrase “you will be purified” can be stated in active form. Alternate translation: [I will purify you as if I were sprinkling you with pure water, and I will cause you to stop worshiping idols] (See also: [Active or Passive](ta:figs-activepassive))
Alternate translation: [all the things that made you unclean]

26.q: I will give you a new heart and a new spirit in your innermost parts, and I will take away the heart of stone from your flesh. For I will give you a heart of flesh
26.note: Yahweh causing the people to no longer be stubborn but to love and serve Yahweh is spoken of as if he will take away their old heart and give them a new heart and spirit.

26.q: a new heart and a new spirit
26.note: Here “heart” and “spirit” represent a person’s thoughts, attitudes, and emotions. See how you translated “heart” and “spirit” in Ezekiel 11:19.
Alternate translation: [within you] or [inside of you]
This speaks of people being stubborn as if their hearts were made of stone. See how you translated “stone heart” in Ezekiel 11:19. Alternate translation: [the heart that is as hard as stone]
People being willing to serve Yahweh is spoken of as if their hearts were soft like flesh. See how you translated this in Ezekiel 11:19. Alternate translation: [a heart that is soft like flesh]

27.q: enable you to walk in my statutes
27.note: A person acting or behaving in a certain way is spoken of is if it were a person walking. See how you translated this in Ezekiel 11:20. Alternate translation: [enable you to obey my statutes]

29.q: For I will save you from all of your uncleanness
29.note: Something that is unacceptable to Yahweh is spoken of as if it were physically unclean. Alternate translation: [For I will save you from everything that made me reject you]
“I will call the grain to come.” This phrase presents the grain as a servant of Yahweh. Alternate translation: [I will cause there to be grain in the land of Israel]

29.q: I will no longer put famine upon you
29.note: Yahweh causing a famine in the land is spoken of as if he put famine on the people. Alternate translation: [I will no longer cause there to be a famine] or [I will no longer cause there to be no food]

30.q: you will no longer bear the shame of famine among the nations
30.note: Experiencing shame is spoken of as if the people had to carry the shame. Alternate translation: [the nations will no longer make you feel ashamed because you suffer from famine]

31.note: SPEAKER is emphasizing a positive meaning by using a negative word, **not**, together with a mild expression that is the opposite of the intended meaning. If it would be helpful in your language, you could emphasize the positive meaning in a strong way. Alternate translation: [disgusting]

32.q: let this be known to you
32.note: “know this” or “you can be sure of this.” Yahweh says this to emphasize that it is not because the people are good that he will restore them. This phrase can be moved to the beginning of the verse.
The words “ashamed” and “disgraced” share similar meanings. Together they emphasize the intensity of the shame. Alternate translation: [So be very ashamed]
Alternate translation: [because of what you do]
Here “house” represents people. Alternate translation: [people of Israel]

34.q: you will plow the ruined land
34.note: Alternate translation: [you will farm the ruined land]

34.q: before the eyes of all who pass by
34.note: The eyes represent sight. Alternate translation: [to those who pass by and see it]

35.note: The word “they” refers to the people who walk through the land of Israel.
Alternate translation: [the ruins that no one lived in]

If your language does not use the passive form in this way, you can state this in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. This could mean: (1) Alternate translation: [that enemies had torn down] or (2) Alternate translation: [that people could not get into]

If your language does not use the passive form in this way, you can state this in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [the people have now rebuilt them and have started living there again]

36.q: that I built up the ruins
36.note: Alternate translation: [and that I built up the cities that enemies had torn down]
Alternate translation: [planted crops in the desolate land]

37.q: I will be asked by the house of Israel
37.note: Here “house” represents people. If your language does not use the passive form in this way, you can state this in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [The people of Israel will ask me] (See also: [Active or Passive](ta:figs-activepassive))

37.q: to increase them like a flock of people
37.note: Yahweh causing the people to multiply greatly and quickly is spoken of as if they were a flock of sheep. Sheep multiply very quickly. Alternate translation: [to make them multiply like a flock of sheep] or [to make the people multiply quickly like sheep]

38.q: Like the flock is set apart for sacrifices, like the flock in Jerusalem at her appointed feasts
38.note: The phrase “is set apart” can be stated in active form. Alternate translation: [Like the great number of sheep that the people set apart for sacrifices or bring to Jerusalem for the appointed feasts]

38.q: so will the ruined cities be filled with flocks of people
38.note: This speaks of the people of Israel as if they were a flock of sheep. If your language does not use the passive form in this way, you can state this in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [so will the great number of people be who will be living in the cities that are now ruined but the people will rebuild] (See also: [Active or Passive](ta:figs-activepassive))
